featured_reviews.name: Divyang Oza
featured_reviews.review_text:
I visited Dakshinayan on a Saturday evening around 4:00 PM, right at the start of their evening hours.

We were able to grab a table easily. The place was a bit loud due to people chatting, but it was still comfortable enough to enjoy the meal.

We quickly ordered a few items — Idli Vada, Molgapodi Idli, Molgapodi Masala Dosa, Mysore Masala Dosa, along with beverages like Filter Coffee and Sugarcane Juice.

The Molgapodi Idli arrived first, and it was excellent. When dipped in the flavorful, well-spiced sambar and paired with the tomato chutney, it was an epic combination. I also took a quick bite from my dad’s Idli Vada plate, which was equally tasty.

Then came the dosas — they were truly incredible. The taste of ghee combined with the hint of podi masala and the flavorful masala filling made them delicious and quite filling. Paired with the spicy onion chutney, it was exactly the kind of evening snack I was looking for.

The Filter Coffee was superb, and the Sugarcane Juice was refreshing and well-balanced.

We ended the meal with Mango Ice Cream, which was freshly prepared at the restaurant. It was delightful, with actual pieces of Alphonso mangoes adding to the authenticity and taste.

Overall, I really enjoyed the meal here and would definitely recommend this place to anyone looking to enjoy authentic South Indian delicacies.

Ambiance and Service

Food and Specialties

Standout recommendations include the Molgapodi Idli generously coated in ghee and gunpowder, alongside their comforting Rasam Vada and crispy Mysore Masala Dosa. featured_reviews.name: Yati Soni
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving authentic, no-frills South Indian food in Juhu, Sri Annapoorna Cafe is an absolute gem. The menu is refreshingly simple, but every item delivers on taste, quality, and authenticity.

The sambhar is rich, perfectly spiced, and feels like it’s straight out of a traditional South Indian kitchen. The benne podi masala dosa is a standout—crispy on the outside, generously layered with butter, and packed with flavorful podi that hits just right.

The idli with rasam is comfort in a plate—soft, fluffy idlis paired with a tangy, soul-warming rasam that you’ll want to keep sipping. And the vada? Crisp on the outside, soft inside, and absolutely worth the hype.

What really sets this place apart is how it sticks to its roots—no unnecessary gimmicks, just honest, traditional flavors done right. Add to that the pocket-friendly pricing, and you’ve got a spot that’s truly worth every rupee.

Simple menu, authentic taste, and consistently good food—definitely a must-visit for South Indian lovers.

Your words about our simple menu, consistency, and no-frills approach are especially encouraging, as that is exactly what we aim to deliver—honest food made with care and quality ingredients.

1.This is the run and owned  by the same family who runs the matunga eatery since day one it opened in vile parle east i started frequenting this place  I must clearly point out my observations for this place
Food is not as perfected like the OG Arya bhavan at matunga i feel that  matunga  has good chefs and service staff to deliver Excellence this vile parle branch offers almost the same menu  but at  times I felt that the food goes haywire chutneys sometimes  are very  well prepared  but some times watery chutneys and half done dosas not done right.

2.i feel  owner should & MUST visit this place atleast 3 times a week though his son and the owner himself know me i feel the service and food here get wonky many  times as they have recently expanded to other branches in sewri chembur too hence staff issue remains a challenge in kitchen as well in service.

3.So the rating 3 is given in comparison with the Original Matunga Arya Bhavan the food otherwise is amazing rite from the masala dosa perfectly made to the Medu vada -is Must try make sure they freshly make it for you when u order it the best perfect medu vada i have ever eaten in mumbai (matunga branch does it right each time everytime) they serve the amazing red green thick freshly made chutneys and perfectly made Sambhar

Thathe idli with podi is perfect

Another hidden gem in the menu is Biscuit Dosa its heaven specially if u like pizzas u will like this Innovatively made dosa styled and made by them.

Idlis are well made nice fluffy perfected with their in-house spl batter u will notice the difference in the first bite itself

They have other variety of dosas like palak dosa Mysore dosa which go well select ur pick

Kanchipuram idli Brahman idli all are good

The best part is they have full ac Restaurant with table service

The service is wobbly which I have complained to the owner once as you have to keep asking people to clean table for water for your food to be served hence I rate service 2star as the staff training is a challenge here getting staff is a bigger challenge in this place hence if they have full strength of staff you might get proper service sometimes they will forget chutneys with dosas hence you will have to ask them for chutneys by the time they get chutney dosa will be over the person who cleans tables may not clean the table properly you may have to ask again for it constantly you will have to ask for water tissue spoon etc ....they may not be proactive it all depends on the staff mood so

While ac works fine washroom is a challenge to use as water soap tissues hygeine are clear issues which owner has to address ASAP

this place  is way above the average south indian Udupi restaurants and its can be termed as a gem for south indian breakfast lovers it does decent "ghati" desi style pizza too few sandwiches freshly made juices and has started chaats

Showstopper is the goti sodas with flavours ,Ananda milk is stocked up and has handmade ice cream which  could definitely be tried chocolate Orange my personal favorite

Coin idli ,butter idli, are all time favorite

Rassam wada is another gem in their menu but have it with pipping hot rasam  and freshly made vada

Their tomato Rasam served here is another favourite's I sometimes come here just to have that however matunga outlet  does it better

Filter coffee is decent served in traditional brass tumbler set with spl sugar

Parking is roadside avoid going on weekends public holidays

Must visit the place after 8.30am before noon on weekdays to avoid  any waiting reservation is not required they are there on swiggy zomato however eating food going there is recommended

Curd rice, bisse bille bhat pav bhaji all is served

Looking for variety seated service with ac  quality food  this is it!!

featured_reviews.review_text:
Malgudi: Great Vibes, Confused Kitchen & Extra Fees
Let’s be real—I wanted to love this place. Walking into Malgudi on SV Road, the vibe is immaculate. It sets you up for a cozy, authentic South Indian experience. But between the kitchen confusion and the final bill, it’s a bit of a rollercoaster.
Here is the unfiltered breakdown:
The Star of the Show
If you go here, do yourself a favor and order the Benne Masala Dosa. It was genuinely too good—crispy, buttery, and exactly what you hope for. The chutney pairing was also on point and very tasty.
The "What happened here?" Section
Unfortunately, the rest of the meal felt like an identity crisis.
• The Sambar Situation: This was weird. The sambar actually tasted different across different dishes. Consistency is key, guys—pick a lane!
• Portions & Options: The menu feels very limited, and the portion sizes are basically a tease. For the price, you expect to leave full, not looking for a snack on the way home.
• Overall Taste: Aside from the Benne Dosa, the general taste could really be improved. It feels like they are holding back flavor.
The Coffee Letdown
For a place with this vibe, you expect the coffee game to be strong. It wasn't.
• Coffee Mocktails: Hard pass. They just felt not worth the price tag.
• Filter Coffee: The ultimate test for a South Indian spot, and they failed it. It tasted average at best and definitely lacked that authentic "kick" you crave.
The Final Pinch
Just when you are questioning the portion sizes vs. the price, the bill arrives. They levy a 5% Service Charge.
Paying extra for "service" when the filter coffee is average and the sambar is inconsistent? That stings.
The Verdict
Go for the Benne Masala Dosa and the aesthetic, but lower your expectations for everything else. It’s a great place to sit, but be ready to pay a premium (plus 5%) for a mixed bag of flavors.

Now that Benne Dosa is so much in trend, I decided to look for a nearby outlet and try it out, so I visited Namma Benne House, Taste the Authenticity of Bengaluru. This outlet is located in Borivali West near Croma.

This is a self service setup with only outdoor seating, so the focus here is clearly on the food. I ordered Ghee Pudi Idli and Benne Plain Dosa.

The Ghee Pudi Idli was served hot and fresh. The texture was very good. It was soft and moist. It was soft, moist, and evenly coated with ghee and plenty of pudi.

The Benne Plain Dosa was not very crispy. It was more on the softer side. I feel it was made using a different style of batter. The fermentation was good. The dosa was cooked evenly. The ghee added richness without making it oily.
It was served with sambar and two types of chutneys, both of which were well balanced and complemented the dosa well. The sambar was delicious.

The menu mentions that potato palya is included with every dosa. I was not served that. This affected the overall experience. The prices are on the higher side, and for a self service outlet, I would have expected slightly better value.

That said, I genuinely appreciated their effort towards sustainability. They are using eco friendly plates and spoons, and I did not notice any plastic being used, which is a thoughtful touch.

If you want to try a Bengaluru style Benne Dosa, you can visit Namma Benne House in Borivali.

Quality – 3.9/5
Quantity – 3.9/5
Service – 3.5/5
Price – ₹400 for 2 people

featured_reviews.name: Rohan Kini
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good place for South Indian food! The seating is open with a small AC section — not sure if it’s open for customers though. They have 2-seater and 4-seater tables, so the place can’t handle a big crowd. It works on a first-come, first-serve basis.

We tried the Set Dosa and Benne Masala Dosa. I was surprised by the white bhaji they served — it was quite tasteless and didn’t go well with the dosa. They should stick to the regular yellow masala. The benne flavor was nice, but the dosa was a bit over-crispy and slightly burnt in parts, which spoiled the taste at times. On the brighter side, the chutney and sambar were perfect — classic South Indian flavor!

The Set Dosa was really good — crispy yet soft and tasty. I went with my friend, and we shared these two items and were completely full. Benne dosas are quite heavy, so order accordingly!

It’s a self-service place, and they call out your token number once the food is ready

featured_reviews.name: Kiyansh Shukla
featured_reviews.review_text:
With multiple popular branches spread across Mumbai—including Kandivali West (Mahavir Nagar), Borivali West, Mira Road, Malad, and several Andheri Metro stations—South Tiffin House has carved out a solid niche for itself. It positions itself as an affordable, fast-casual quick service brand.
Depending on the outlet you visit, the setup ranges from small, cozy indoor seating spaces to minimalist, metro-station grab-and-go counters. It is designed for quick meals, casual weekend breakfasts, or late-night street food cravings.
The Food: Traditional Roots Meet Fusion Twists
The menu is a massive playground that balances classic Udupi-style staples with experimental fusion items that cater heavily to Mumbai’s street food culture.
The Must-Try Classics:
The undisputed crowd-pleasers here are the Thatte Idlis. They are large, plate-sized, pillowy-soft Karnataka-style idlis. Getting them as the Ghee Podi Thatte Idli is highly recommended; the generous dousing of aromatic ghee and flavorful gun powder (podi) is incredibly satisfying. Their classic Mysore Masala Dosa and crispy Medu Vada are also solid, reliable picks.
The Fusion Experiments:
If you like adventurous street food flavors, they offer unique options like Sri Lankan Curry Paniyaram, Peri Peri Mini Idlis, and Pizza Uttapams. The Sri Lankan style dishes featuring rich coconut-milk based flavors are a pleasant surprise for a fast-casual menu.
Filter Coffee:
No South Indian meal is complete without it, and their strong, aromatic filter coffee serves as the perfect finishing touch.
Areas for Improvement
While the food taste is generally well-received and offers great value for money, consistency can vary across branches and platforms:
In-House vs. Delivery: Diners frequently note that eating fresh, piping-hot food at the restaurant is a far superior experience. On delivery apps, the sambhar and chutneys can occasionally arrive running a bit cold or watery, and crispy dosas inevitably soften in transit.
The Sambhar Dynamic: If you prefer highly authentic, deeply traditional, tangy Tamil-style sambhar, you might find their version leans slightly on the sweeter side to match local Mumbai preferences.
